title: Find the long task in a trace
purpose: Find the long task in the Main track, read the interaction's INP, and see how CPU throttling and a split task change it.
sequence_reason: Each step depends on the one before: the throttled recording shows the long task, the long task explains the slow interaction, and the fix changes the next recording.
summary: A guided walkthrough of one example trace: at 20x CPU slowdown a 15 ms click handler becomes a 300 ms long task, the interaction takes 360 ms, and splitting the work so the page paints first brings it down to 100 ms. The numbers are an example.
explanation: CPU throttling makes main-thread work longer, so a handler that is short on a fast laptop can become a long task that delays the next paint.

learning_check.question: Why can a click handler that takes 15 ms on your laptop still give a poor INP for real users?
learning_check.answer: On a slower CPU the same work takes longer; at 20x slowdown it becomes a 300 ms long task that delays the next paint.

scenes.heading: Find the long task
scenes.narration: Here is one example trace of a single click.

visual.subtitle: An example trace, recorded at 20x CPU slowdown

scenes.heading: Read the flame chart
scenes.narration: The Main track is a flame chart. The x-axis is time. The y-axis is the call stack. Events on top cause the events below.

items: Events on top cause the events below

scenes.heading: One long task
scenes.narration: At 20x slowdown the click handler takes 300 milliseconds. A red triangle marks it, and the part over 50 milliseconds is red.

scenes.heading: The interaction's time
scenes.narration: The Interactions track splits the click into input delay, processing time and presentation delay. Here they add up to 360 milliseconds.

visual.expression: 360 ms = 20 ms input delay + 300 ms processing + 40 ms presentation delay

terms.note: a timer task was still running
the click handler, a long task

scenes.heading: Why throttle the CPU
scenes.narration: Without throttling, the same handler takes 15 milliseconds and INP is 18. The 20x slowdown shows what a slower device feels.

visual.verdict: Same code, slower CPU, longer tasks.

scenes.heading: Split the work
scenes.narration: Before: one 300 millisecond task. After: update the page in 40 milliseconds, then yield. The browser paints, the rest runs in short tasks, and INP drops to 100.

visual.verdict: No task over 50 ms; INP under 200 ms.

scenes.heading: Layout shifts track
scenes.narration: The Layout shifts track shows each shift as a purple diamond, grouped in clusters. Keep CLS at 0.1 or less.
